Stated Claim / Post Context:
US prison population drops 25%, Malaysia restores parliamentary independence, bus stop rain gardens

In today's edition: the prison population in the US is falling as inmates age out of incarceration and are not replaced by newcomers; Malaysia strengthens its separation between powers; and New York's bus stop rain gardens are reducing flooding while cooling down shelters on hot days.

Actual Article Body:
Elizabeth Jacyshyn-Owen | Posted on October 9, 2026 |

Photo: Hoseung Han/Unsplash (CC0)

In today’s edition: the prison population in the US is falling as inmates age out of incarceration and are not replaced by newcomers; Malaysia strengthens its separation between powers; and New York’s bus stop rain gardens are reducing flooding while cooling down shelters on hot days.

Not only is the US prison population declining at an accelerating rate, but prison admission rates themselves are predicted to fall an additional 50% within the next two decades. Since 2000, prison admission rates for people ages 18 to 30 have already fallen 53%.

Source: phys.org

The Parliamentary Services Act 2025 has officially come into effect, essentially reinstating the autonomy of Parliament with a dedicated parliamentary service. In practical terms, it furthers the Malaysian government’s separation of democratic powers and the system of checks and balances.

Source: Malay Mail

More than 4.3 million Australian households now have rooftop solar, driving record amounts of renewable energy into the grid. In a first, sunshine and wind met 80.4% of demand on Australia’s main power grid on Saturday, setting a new high bar for renewable electricity.

Source: The Guardian

As emerging economies and global living standards rise, it might be reasonable to assume that the world is in for another fossil fuel boom, but the data say otherwise. Countries from Southeast Asia to Sub-Saharan Africa aren’t investing in fossil fuels as the West did; they’re looking towards electricity powered by renewables.

Source: Deutsche Welle

Since coming into power, the Trump administration has decimated funding to gender-affirming care in the region by striking deals with major hospital systems. Now, Mayor Zohran Mamdani has announced a $15 million investment in gender-affirming care initiatives, with the first $9 million to be distributed among local organisations providing life-saving support to the city’s young people.

Source: Gothamist

City officials hope the environmentally friendly redesign could spruce up transit stops across the five boroughs. The green roofs feature native grasses and other vegetation, can absorb 16 gallons of rainwater to reduce flooding during heavy rainstorms, and could also cool down the shelter for riders waiting for buses on hot days.

Source: Gothamist

You probably know at least a handful of friends or family members who didn’t vote in the last election. Now, Patagonia wants to offer you $100 to nudge three of them to vote in November, regardless of which party they opt for. After you (consensually) enter the details for those you want to encourage to vote, the platform creates a personalised voting plan.

Source: Fast Company

Although long-term protection ultimately depends on limiting the warming of the seas, covering vulnerable corals during extreme high temperatures could reduce heat stress by reducing the intense sunlight and ultraviolet radiation that can make bleaching worse.

Source: Euronews

As Africa’s first Indigenous-owned elephant sanctuary, Reteti is part of a growing grassroots movement putting local communities at the heart of conservation. It spreads the message that the future of wildlife is inseparable from the livelihoods of the people who share the environment, while also letting Samburu women gain independence, income and a voice

Source: Positive News

Across Europe, community-led campaigns are finding unique ways to support men’s mental health as waiting lists for care continue to grow. These include barbershop and tattoo studio therapists, nature-based rehabilitation programmes, and social prescribing.

Source: Euronews
